task.title: Decide whether read-path scenarios carry duration targets
task.description:
The 2026-07-30 scaling work added a cold cli-list read scenario to the benchmark registry. It deliberately carries no duration target, because the approved 200 ms cold budget was established for mutations. Decide whether read paths should carry targets of their own.

Investigated 2026-08-06 at commit c453596.

cli-list is still the only read-path scenario, and its target is nil (internal/perf/scenarios.go:912-915), pinned by TestColdListScenarioHasNoApprovedDurationTarget (internal/perf/list_scenario_test.go:65). README:30-32 and :525-526 already state that it is reported descriptively with no approved target. The validation scenarios, which are read-ish, do carry targets (10 s, 500 ms, 1 s at internal/perf/validation_scenarios.go).

Measured headroom is large: medians of 59.44, 68.83, and 84.84 ms at 100, 500, and 1000 tasks (commit 725a2838) against a 200 ms mutation budget. Either outcome is therefore cheap, and neither is blocked by anything in the harness.

Worth folding into the decision: the hot agent loop currently has no read scenarios at all. There is no cli-next or cli-show in the registry, and next fetches before answering, so it plausibly lands in the autosync latency class rather than the local one. That work is tracked separately, and whatever target policy is chosen here should be the policy those scenarios adopt, rather than being decided twice.

Acceptance: document the decision in docs/performance/README.md, and either attach an approved target that reports are auto-classified against, or state that read scenarios remain descriptive and say why. Update list_scenario_test.go if a target is added, since it currently pins the absence.
